quests.instruction: Say a synonym that fits the meaning in this sentence.
quests.hint: Someone owns a shop and makes the day-to-day decisions.
quests.explanation: In this sentence "run" means to be in charge of a business. "Manages" and "operates" are the closest, "oversees" suggests supervising, and "looks after" is a friendlier phrase. It has nothing to do with moving on foot, and it's different from a road that "runs" along a coast.
quests.textToSpeak: She *runs* a small bakery downtown.

quests.instruction: Say a word with the same meaning in this context.
quests.hint: Imagine a company is planning a yearly gathering and someone asks where it will take place.
quests.explanation: "Hold" here means to organize an event, not to grip something in your hand. "Host" and "conduct" are formal, "have" is the simple everyday word, and "stage" suggests a bigger, more organized event. Compare "the hall can hold 500 people", where a different verb is needed.
quests.textToSpeak: The company will *hold* its annual meeting in June.

quests.instruction: Give a natural synonym for the highlighted word.
quests.hint: A bank is telling a customer when the replacement will arrive.
quests.explanation: Think about "issue": it is a formal verb meaning to officially give or send out. "Provide", "give", "send" and "supply" all work in different contexts, and "send" is very natural for cards. "Issue" can also mean a problem or an edition of a magazine, but not here.
quests.textToSpeak: The bank will *issue* a new card next week.

quests.instruction: Say a word that matches the tone of the sentence.
quests.hint: Think of it this way: a teacher lets students avoid work and doesn't follow up.
quests.explanation: Notice that "soft" describes a person who is too lenient here, not something that feels smooth. "Lenient" is the direct synonym, "permissive" and "indulgent" suggest allowing too much, and "easygoing" is friendlier and less critical.
quests.textToSpeak: The teacher is too *soft*, so the students never do homework.

quests.instruction: Give a synonym that sounds natural in this situation.
quests.hint: After a long flight, someone is completely worn out and sleeping through everything.
quests.explanation: "Deep" as a description of sleep means heavy and undisturbed. "Sound" is the very common partner word, "heavy" suggests it's hard to wake him, and "profound" is formal. It's not the same "deep" as in "a deep voice" or "deep water".
quests.textToSpeak: After the long flight, he fell into a *deep* sleep.

quests.instruction: Replace the highlighted word with a synonym.
quests.hint: Two runners crossed the line at almost exactly the same time.
quests.explanation: "Close" in a race means the difference is tiny. "Tight" and "even" are the natural choices, and "narrow" is often used for a small gap. It isn't a synonym for "near" or for a close friend.
quests.textToSpeak: The race was so *close* that nobody knew who won.

quests.instruction: Say a synonym that fits the meaning in this sentence.
quests.hint: Two friends have been arguing about a small problem, and one asks why they are bothering.
quests.explanation: "Point" here means the reason for doing something. "Purpose" is the direct match, "use" is common in spoken English, "sense" is slightly old-fashioned, and "value" points to the benefit. "Point" can also mean a moment or the sharp tip of a pencil.
quests.textToSpeak: What's the *point* of arguing about this?

quests.instruction: Say another word with the same meaning.
quests.hint: Imagine a group of friends is taking turns choosing entertainment for the evening.
quests.explanation: In this sentence, "turn" is a noun here and means the opportunity that belongs to someone. "Go" is common and casual (especially British), while "chance" and "opportunity" also work, and "opportunity" is the most formal. The verb "turn" means to change direction or become.
quests.textToSpeak: It's your *turn* to choose the movie.

quests.instruction: Say a different word that keeps the same meaning.
quests.hint: Suppose a waiter is describing a really special drink on the wine list.
quests.explanation: "Fine" here means excellent quality. "Excellent" is the common synonym, "superior" is formal, "premium" suggests it is high-end, and "high-quality" is direct. This isn't the "fine" of "I'm fine", or a fine you pay for breaking a rule.
quests.textToSpeak: This restaurant serves *fine* wine.

quests.instruction: Say a word with the same meaning in this context.
quests.hint: Picture this: you're telling a friend you can't meet because your calendar is crammed with tasks.
quests.explanation: Look at "heavy" first: it describes a schedule with too much on it, not something that weighs a lot. "Packed" is the natural everyday choice, "full" is simple, "demanding" suggests the work is hard, and "busy" is a plain and common option.
quests.textToSpeak: I have a *heavy* schedule this week.

quests.instruction: Replace the highlighted word with a synonym.
quests.hint: You slept badly because your bed pushes back rather than giving under your weight.
quests.explanation: "Hard" here describes a surface that doesn't give way. "Firm" is the polite, positive word for mattresses, "stiff" and "rigid" are more negative, and "unyielding" is a formal way to say the same. It is not "difficult", and it isn't "a hard worker".
quests.textToSpeak: I don't like this bed. The mattress is too *hard*.

quests.instruction: Say a synonym that fits the meaning in this sentence.
quests.hint: You're stuck at an airport with a long wait and no work to do.
quests.explanation: "Pass" here means to use time. "Spend" is the simplest, "fill" shows the time would be empty otherwise, "kill" is informal and very common, and "while away" is a longer phrase for using free time in a relaxed way. It's not the "pass" of "I'll pass", meaning decline.
quests.textToSpeak: We played cards to *pass* the time.

quests.instruction: Say another word with the same meaning.
quests.hint: Hundreds of people work in a large building where products are made.
quests.explanation: "Plant" here is a place where goods are produced. "Factory" is the most common word, "facility" is more formal and general, and "mill" is used for particular products. It isn't a garden plant or the action of putting seeds in the ground.
quests.textToSpeak: The *plant* employs about five hundred workers.

quests.instruction: Give a natural synonym for the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Think about the land beside flowing water, not a place for money.
quests.explanation: "Bank" here means the land alongside a river. "Shore" is the everyday choice, "edge" is simple and general, and "embankment" is more technical and often describes a raised slope. The "bank" where people keep money is a different meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: We had a picnic on the river *bank*.

quests.instruction: Say a synonym for the highlighted word.
quests.hint: A pet moves suddenly and with energy from the ground to a higher surface.
quests.explanation: The key word is "sprang", which means to jump or move quickly and suddenly. "Jumped" is simple, "leapt" is a strong, graceful jump, "bounded" suggests springy steps, and "vaulted" suggests jumping over or onto something. It is not the season or a metal coil.
quests.textToSpeak: The cat *sprang* onto the counter.

quests.instruction: Say a word that could replace the highlighted one here.
quests.hint: A road keeps beside the edge of the sea for a long distance.
quests.explanation: Here, "runs" describes the direction or length of a road. "Stretches" and "extends" both show a long distance, "goes" is casual, and "follows" suggests the road matches the shape of the coast. This is not "run a business" or "run a race".
quests.textToSpeak: The road *runs* along the coast for fifty miles.

quests.instruction: Say a synonym that fits the meaning in this sentence.
quests.hint: Think of it this way: an event organizer checks the size of a venue before booking it.
quests.explanation: "Hold" here means to have space for. "Seat" means to provide seats, "accommodate" is formal and general, "fit" is casual, and "take" is a simple, everyday choice. It's not the "hold" of "hold a meeting".
quests.textToSpeak: This hall can *hold* five hundred people.

quests.instruction: Say a different word that keeps the same meaning.
quests.hint: You're at a newsstand and you're talking about the newest version of a magazine.
quests.explanation: "Issue" here means a version published at a set time. "Edition" is the most formal choice, "copy" refers to the physical item, and "number" is used in British English for a particular issue. It's not "a problem" or "to issue" something formally.
quests.textToSpeak: I read the latest *issue* of the magazine.

quests.instruction: Say a word that matches the tone of the sentence.
quests.hint: You need to speak in a way that doesn't wake a sleeping baby.
quests.explanation: Start with "soft": it describes a voice that isn't loud or harsh. "Quiet" and "low" fit most simply, "gentle" adds kindness, and "muted" suggests the sound has been reduced. It's not the "soft" of "too soft on students", which means lenient.
quests.textToSpeak: She spoke in a *soft* voice so she wouldn't wake the baby.

quests.instruction: Say a synonym for the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Think of it this way: you're describing a radio host whose voice sits at the bottom of the pitch range.
quests.explanation: To choose well, note that "deep" describes a low pitch here. "Low" is the everyday word, "bass" is a musical term, "rich" describes fullness, and "resonant" suggests a voice that carries sound well. It isn't "deep sleep", which means heavy sleep.
quests.textToSpeak: He has a *deep* voice, like a radio host.

quests.instruction: Give a synonym that sounds natural in this situation.
quests.hint: You've entered a room where the air feels heavy and nothing has moved for hours.
quests.explanation: "Close" as a description of air means without enough fresh air. "Stuffy" is the everyday word, "airless" is more direct, and "muggy" suggests warm, damp air. It isn't the meaning of "near" or "a close race".
quests.textToSpeak: The room was *close* and smelled of old coffee.

quests.instruction: Say a synonym that fits the meaning in this sentence.
quests.hint: Here's the scene: you're telling a story about the instant you noticed that something had gone wrong.
quests.explanation: "Point" here means a particular time in a process. "Moment" is the everyday word, "stage" suggests part of a longer sequence, "time" is simple, and "juncture" is formal. It isn't the purpose of doing something.
quests.textToSpeak: At that *point*, I realized I had made a mistake.

quests.instruction: Give a natural synonym for the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Overnight, the weather changed and temperatures fell sharply.
quests.explanation: "Turn" as a verb here means to become. "Became" is neutral, "grew" is literary, "got" is casual, and "went" is common with weather and colors. It's not the noun "turn", meaning someone's chance to do something.
quests.textToSpeak: The weather *turned* cold overnight.

quests.instruction: Say another word with the same meaning.
quests.hint: You parked in a place where you weren't allowed, and you're telling a friend about it.
quests.explanation: "Fine" here is a noun: money you pay as punishment. "Penalty" is the general word, "ticket" is very common for parking, "citation" is more formal and American, and "charge" is a broader term. It isn't the adjective "fine", meaning okay or excellent.
quests.textToSpeak: I got a *fine* for parking in the wrong place.

quests.instruction: Say a word with the same meaning in this context.
quests.hint: You canceled your plans because of very strong rain.
quests.explanation: "Heavy" describes rain that falls strongly. "Torrential" is much stronger, "intense" is neutral, and "hard" is very common in spoken English. It's not a heavy schedule or a heavy bag.
quests.textToSpeak: We couldn't go out because of the *heavy* rain.

quests.instruction: Replace the highlighted word with a synonym.
quests.hint: You're describing a colleague who works with great effort and never misses a target.
quests.explanation: "Hard" in "hard worker" describes effort, not difficulty or firmness. "Diligent", "industrious" and "dedicated" are all common, and "tireless" suggests an amazing level of energy. It has nothing to do with the mattress sense of "hard".
quests.textToSpeak: He's a *hard* worker and never misses a deadline.

quests.instruction: Say a synonym that fits the meaning in this sentence.
quests.hint: You're telling a friend that you succeeded in an official test on the first attempt.
quests.explanation: "Pass" here means to succeed in a test. "Cleared" is common in Indian English and elsewhere, "got through" is casual, and "made it through" suggests some effort or difficulty. It isn't "pass the time" or "I'll pass".
quests.textToSpeak: She *passed* her driving test on the first try.

quests.instruction: Say a synonym for the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Imagine a family started a small vegetable garden in spring.
quests.explanation: "Plant" here is a verb meaning to put seeds or young plants in the ground. "Sowed" is the standard word for seeds, "put in" is casual, and "set out" is often used for young plants. It is not the factory sense of "plant".
quests.textToSpeak: We *planted* tomatoes in April.

quests.instruction: Say a word that could replace the highlighted one here.
quests.hint: Two people had a loud disagreement at home, and you're describing it to a friend.
quests.explanation: "Row" rhymes with "cow" here and is British. "Argument" is the general word, "quarrel" suggests a personal disagreement, "dispute" is more formal, and "spat" is a small or short one. It's not a line of seats or the act of moving a boat.
quests.textToSpeak: They had a *row* about money last night.

quests.instruction: Give a natural synonym for the highlighted word.
quests.hint: You're describing a band that was expected at a festival but didn't come.
quests.explanation: "Appear" here means to arrive or be present. "Show up" and "turn up" are natural spoken phrases, and "arrive" is more general and formal. "Appear" can also mean "seem", as in "she appears tired", but that isn't the meaning here.
quests.textToSpeak: The band didn't *appear* at the festival.
